articles.title: Quad9 pulled their DNS service from France
articles.summary: Quad9 pulled their DNS service from France

top_comments: I've set up an open Quad9 DNS proxy for anyone in France who'd like a (fairly) drop-in replacement. All it does is cache and forward DNS requests to Quad9, and it's set up to work with DoH, DoT, Do53 UDP+TCP, IPv4 and IPv6. DoT: quad9.domainintelligence.uk DoH: https://quad9.domainintelligence.uk/dns-query 213.171.214.215 2a00:da00:f47f:3600::1 DoT: quad9-unfiltered.domainintelligence.uk DoH: https://quad9-unfiltered.domainintelligence.uk/dns-query 213.165.84.229 2a00:da00:f47f:3600::2 It was frustrating for me this morning to find out that my servers were getting REFUSED replies from Quad9, I didn't even realise that they were in France (I just knew it was the EU). Let me know if there's any issues.

Discussion (1382 points, 1 month ago, 481 comments) https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50195959Or Quad9's withdrawal from France: A canary in the coal mine (911 points, 1 week ago, 457 comments) https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50538994
We're really underselling the fact the French government made DNS caches illegal? This wasn't Quad9's decision.

Unless I'm totally mistaken, this scores equivalent to opus 4.6 (released feb 2026) on SWE-bench verified. I just don't see this as deadly to the production of games the way others do. GTA 6 is a monumental human achievement in video games - in fact it's arguably one of the largest artistic endeavors ever undertaken. If numbers are to believed, it has also already made around $4 billion against a $1-2 billion budget. It is massively profitable, and doubtless will become more so as DLC and a real PC port are released.I see this, instead, as a continuation of the usual pushback against the lockdown of entertainment to certain media. I personally haven't bought the game yet because I don't have or intend to buy an Xbox! It's deeply frustrating that everyone else will get to experience it before me because I didn't want to spend hundreds of dollars on a console!But I will probably still buy it when it comes out on PC, even if this port works.

For the general picture: the Xbox version of the game was leaked by Cyberleek - first the resources, then the game binary.Because modern Xbox is very close to a Windows PC with some extra Xbox stuff, running the actual game code isn't hard, it's mostly about compatibility and graphics, plus the binary doesn't have any special DRM/obfuscation.The current projects (xcl and VIctory) basically take a Wine-like approach. The main problems they have to solve, as I understand:- The game ships with raw RDNA 2 shaders, so the projects have to translate that to another format, e.g. DXIL for DirectX 12, and compile those shaders. So you need a good translation/recompilation pipeline, if it's bad, the shaders will be bloated and perform poorly- Xbox has unified memory, while most PCs do not, so you have to add a lot of workarounds and book-keeping for the game to work properly with that- Xbox's DirectX 12 differs from the normal Windows one in some ways, and the game uses Xbox-specific texture formats with DirectStorageI just wanted to share this because there's a lot of misconceptions going around about this being a "recomp" or something like that. Decompiling the entire binary (it's about 100MB of real executable machine code) will be a much bigger effort than getting this binary to run.

top_comments: Hello my old friend PRNG.”The actor scanned and began exploitation against the HFS server. Each POST to the HFS loginSrp1 endpoint returns a new signed session cookie containing a “sid” value drawn from JavaScript’s Math.random() function. Through conducting several logins in succession, the actor collected enough output to reconstruct the internal state of the [Node.js] V8 PRNG algorithm, and thus recover an HFS session-cookie signing key, then forge a signed admin session cookie. This allows the attacker to login as admin without a password.”

Buckle up, this is just the beginning of the end. ATM only more sophisticated cyber criminals or state actors use LLMs to penetrate, but soon the chaotic landscape of 100.000s of cyber criminals will just use compute to prompt models to "Make me as much money as possible" , with the result of these models/swarms attacking any online service including critical infrastructure.

2026-10-02 13:17:45 UTC - The actor scanned and began exploitation against the HFS server. top_comments: > We gave GPT‑6.2 the three-dimensional structures of five target proteins and marked where we wanted a minibinder to attach. It then wrote code to create three-dimensional designs for potential minibinders, without using specialized protein AI models.The ability to write code is basically the superpower for these models.As long as what you need to do to make progress is write better code, they will do better at the task.The last 30 years has been making more and more things run using code instead of any other mechanism (music, illustration, vfx).Even math, the models were worse off before Lean was accepted as output.

articles.summary: Heart attack and stroke risk detectable decades in advance

top_comments: The main risk factors they investigated were blood pressure, cholesterol (HDL and total), inflammation (CRP), BMI, troponin, and diabetes/smoking status.Many of these numbers can combined into a prediction of your 30-year heart disease risk using the PREVENT equations: https://app.empirical.health/app/prevent-risk-calculator-for...The good news is that most of these risk factors are very modifiable. We have medications that can reduce LDL cholesterol by 80%, for example, while also lowering inflammation by about 37%.
